label: For two distinct contributors of one exercised record in a coherent exercise, where that record is…
paraphrase: For two distinct contributors of one exercised record in a coherent exercise, where that record is jointly sufficient, at least one holds: a contributor is redundant, or each occurs at an allowed scenario without the other and without the effect while the pair has a common source or is a brute coincidence by the stated definition. A four-way form adds mutual fit; branches may overlap and exclusivity is not claimed. All labels are relative to one scenario space and event carrier. Under those hypotheses mutual fit makes both contributors redundant; if both are needed, the pair does not fit and neither occurs at every allowed scenario; a contributor occurring at every allowed scenario is redundant; if all members occur at every allowed scenario so does the effect; an event sufficing for each member suffices for the effect; and an event at every allowed scenario sufficing for a contributor excludes needing both. If an event suffices for each contributor and both are needed, each contributor occurs at some allowed scenario without that event. Denying mutual fit between distinct contributors of one record that occur at every allowed scenario is equivalent to that record having at most one such contributor, so that denial is not independent of a per-record at-most-one. Coordination, joint sufficiency, one contributor being an exercised source, and needing both force the brute branch; five explicit controls, one per member with the brute denial as fifth, keep the other four. With every allowed scenario matching an accessible world a contributor of a jointly sufficient coordinated pair with both needed is not necessary at the base world. Coexistence without coordination, compatibility without coexistence, coordination without sufficiency, and sufficiency without Supply are each witnessed. Fixed models: two exercised sources with Supply of every event, no least event, redundant contributors, an effect necessary and a further event contingent in a matching overlay; the #735 plural fixture, both needed and brute, whose scenario space is not matched by worlds of either #735 overlay, which on restriction to the actual scenario has mutual fit and matches the all-necessary overlay; one least source with a brute needed pair; and a pair with a common source and both needed, at one setting with two sources and no least event, at the other with one least source. Two analyst readings of ST I q.11 a.3's third proof are tested: the pairwise reading excludes a source as a coordinated contributor and holds with two sources; the total reading yields at most one exercised source outright. This establishes consequences in the encoded scenario semantics, not metaphysical possibility, productive adequacy or any root premise.
